prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1150; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed collision in a shopping center parking lot. The claimant reports a knee injury and says she was seated in the vehicle when it was struck while backing out of a space. The claimant is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Photos from the scene show the rear quarter panel damage described by the other driver.

Entry 3: Other driver's statement matches the account given by the claimant and the witnesses on how the accident happened. The driver is confirmed as a household member of the policyholder and is covered under the policy.

Entry 4: Claimant was contacted by phone and repeated the same account of the collision, including the sequence of events and where she was seated. No inconsistencies noted between this call and the initial report.

Entry 5: Claimant reports knee pain starting the same day, with the injury consistent in location and force with the impact described. No prior injury to the same knee is known from available records.

Entry 6: Medical records show treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and reduced visits as the claimant's knee improved. Treatment appears to be tapering off at this stage.

Entry 7: Vehicle inspection found no earlier damage to the vehicle, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start date. It is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage came from this impact, so the repair estimate is being reviewed line by line.

Entry 8: Claim is pending completion of the damage review and final medical summary. Current findings support the accident occurring as reported, and the file is being routed for settlement evaluation once the open items are closed.
